concepts.name: Regions and Availability Zones
concepts.summary: Explain that a region is a geographic area made of multiple isolated availability zones and why resources are placed in a specific region.

concepts.name: Console and account root user
concepts.summary: Recognise how to sign in to the console, find services, and know that the root user is a special all-powerful identity to be protected.

concepts.name: EC2 instances and AMIs
concepts.summary: Describe an EC2 instance as a virtual server launched from an AMI with a chosen instance type.

concepts.name: S3 buckets and objects
concepts.summary: Explain that S3 stores objects identified by keys inside globally uniquely named buckets rather than files in a filesystem.

concepts.name: IAM users and permissions
concepts.summary: Understand that IAM controls who can do what in an account and that new users start with no permissions.

concepts.name: Managed service categories
concepts.summary: Name which AWS service fits each broad role: RDS and DynamoDB for databases, Lambda for serverless code, CloudFront for content delivery, Route 53 for DNS, CloudWatch for monitoring.

concepts.name: Pay-as-you-go billing and Free Tier
concepts.summary: Understand that resources incur charges while running or stored and that the Free Tier has limits.

misconceptions.text: Resources created in one region automatically appear and work in every other region.
Stopping or ignoring a resource means AWS charges nothing for it.
The root user should be used for everyday administration.

concepts.name: AWS CLI configuration and use
concepts.summary: Configure credentials and a default region with profiles and run commands such as listing buckets or describing instances.

concepts.name: Security groups
concepts.summary: Write inbound and outbound rules that allow only needed ports and sources, knowing groups are stateful allow-lists.

concepts.name: Launching and connecting to EC2
concepts.summary: Launch an instance with a key pair and security group, connect over SSH, and stop, start or terminate it.

concepts.name: S3 access and storage classes
concepts.summary: Upload and retrieve objects, keep buckets private by default, enable versioning, and choose a storage class by access pattern.

concepts.name: IAM policies and groups
concepts.summary: Attach policies with Effect, Action and Resource to groups and users to grant least privilege for simple tasks.

concepts.name: Basic RDS and DynamoDB use
concepts.summary: Create a managed relational database or a DynamoDB table and connect an application to it.

concepts.name: CloudWatch metrics and alarms
concepts.summary: View built-in metrics and logs and set an alarm on a threshold such as CPU utilisation.

concepts.name: Simple Lambda functions
concepts.summary: Write and invoke a small function triggered by an event such as an S3 upload.

misconceptions.text: Opening a security group to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports is an acceptable way to get things working.
Putting access keys in code or on an instance is a normal way to authenticate.
Data on an EC2 instance's instance store or terminated root volume is always preserved.

concepts.name: VPC design with subnets and routing
concepts.summary: Build a VPC with public and private subnets across AZs, route tables, an internet gateway and NAT gateway.

concepts.name: IAM roles and temporary credentials
concepts.summary: Analyse when to use roles with trust policies so services and applications get temporary credentials instead of long-lived keys.

concepts.name: Load balancing and Auto Scaling
concepts.summary: Distribute traffic across instances in multiple AZs and scale capacity by policy using health checks.

concepts.name: Route 53 routing and DNS records
concepts.summary: Configure hosted zones and records with alias targets and choose simple, weighted, latency or failover routing.

concepts.name: CloudFront distribution with S3 origin
concepts.summary: Serve content through CloudFront with caching behaviours, origin access control and HTTPS.

concepts.name: RDS high availability and backups
concepts.summary: Distinguish Multi-AZ failover from read replicas and plan automated backups and restores.

concepts.name: DynamoDB key and access design
concepts.summary: Choose partition and sort keys from access patterns and pick on-demand or provisioned capacity.

concepts.name: Logs-based troubleshooting with CloudWatch
concepts.summary: Use logs, metrics and alarms together to diagnose failures in deployed applications.

misconceptions.text: A subnet is public simply because it is named public, regardless of its route table.
A Multi-AZ RDS standby can be used to serve read traffic and improve read performance.
DynamoDB can be modelled like a relational database and queried flexibly on any attribute efficiently.

concepts.name: Least-privilege policy evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how identity policies, resource policies, boundaries and organisation SCPs combine, with explicit deny winning, and tighten policies accordingly.

concepts.name: Multi-AZ resilient architecture
concepts.summary: Assess an architecture for single points of failure and choose redundancy across AZs and regions to meet availability goals.

concepts.name: Infrastructure as code with CloudFormation
concepts.summary: Define environments as templates, review change sets, and reason about stack updates and drift.

concepts.name: Serverless event-driven design
aliases: Lambda with SQS SNS API Gateway
concepts.summary: Judge when to use Lambda with queues, topics and APIs, accounting for concurrency, timeouts and cold starts.

concepts.name: Encryption and key management
aliases: encryption at rest and in transit
concepts.summary: Evaluate use of KMS keys, key policies and TLS to protect data in S3, RDS and DynamoDB.

concepts.name: Cost analysis and optimisation
concepts.summary: Compare on-demand, Savings Plans and Spot options, right-size resources, and use cost tools to find waste.

concepts.name: Private connectivity and VPC endpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse ways to connect VPCs and reach AWS services privately without traversing the internet.

concepts.name: Observability and audit trails
concepts.summary: Combine metrics, logs, traces and CloudTrail records to detect problems and investigate changes.

misconceptions.text: An Allow in any attached policy is enough to grant access even if another policy explicitly denies it.
Spreading instances across multiple AZs alone makes an application fully highly available.
Serverless functions scale without limit and cost less than other options in every workload.

concepts.name: Multi-account governance strategy
concepts.summary: Design an account structure with organisational units, SCP guardrails, centralised logging and identity federation.

concepts.name: Disaster recovery strategy selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate backup-restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active designs against RPO, RTO and cost.

concepts.name: Well-Architected trade-off review
concepts.summary: Critique a workload across the pillars and justify trade-offs between reliability, security, performance, cost and operations.

concepts.name: Global architecture design
concepts.summary: Create multi-region designs combining Route 53, CloudFront and replicated data stores, accounting for consistency and failover.

concepts.name: Secure CI/CD and deployment pipelines
concepts.summary: Design automated pipelines with safe rollout strategies, scoped deployment roles and rollback.

concepts.name: Threat detection and incident response
concepts.summary: Evaluate detective controls and construct response runbooks for compromised credentials or exposed resources.

concepts.name: Scaling limits and performance tuning
concepts.summary: Diagnose bottlenecks from quotas, throttling and data distribution and redesign to remove them.

misconceptions.text: Having Multi-AZ resources removes the need for a cross-region disaster recovery plan.
Active-active multi-region is always the best design regardless of cost and complexity.
Tight perimeter controls make detective monitoring and incident runbooks unnecessary.
